UGANDAN TERROIR

Three Distinct Growing Belts: Volcanic Arabica and Indigenous Robusta

Uganda is uniquely endowed with high-altitude volcanic microclimates for specialty Arabica and equatorial rainforest conditions for indigenous Canephora.

Eastern Uganda 1,600 to 2,200 MASL

Mount Elgon (Bugisu)

An extinct shield volcano on the Kenya-Uganda border. Rich mineral volcanic loam, ample rainfall, and cloud cover produce dense, complex Arabica cherries.

Key Grades: Bugisu AA, Bugisu A, PB
Processing: Fully Washed, Sun-Dried
View Bugisu Lots
Western Uganda 1,700 to 2,300 MASL

Rwenzori Mountains

The legendary Mountains of the Moon along the Congo border. Glacial runoff and steep terraced farms provide the foundation for slow natural processing.

Key Grades: Specialty Naturals (86+ SCA)
Processing: Extended Natural, African Beds
View Rwenzori Micro-Lots
Central & South 1,100 to 1,450 MASL

Central Robusta Belt

The native home of wild Coffea canephora. Grown under evergreen shade in Masaka and Mubende. Our Screen 18 selection delivers dense, crema-rich espresso components.

Key Grades: Screen 18 Extra Large, Screen 15
Processing: Polished Natural & Washed
View Robusta Specs

Mount Elgon Bugisu AA

KAMPALA EXPORT MILL

Dry Milling Infrastructure at Plot 45 Industrial Area

Our central export milling and logistics hub in Kampala processes up to 15,000 metric tons of export-grade coffee annually. Designed to meet international food safety protocols, uniform bean density, moisture precision, and defect-free lots.

Optical Color Sorting

High-speed monochromatic and bichromatic cameras reject insect-damaged and defective beans.

Gravimetric Density Tables

Separates lower-density seeds to ensure uniform roasting expansion.

Moisture Controlled Bays

All dry parchment and green lots stored strictly between 10.5% and 12.0% moisture.

Hermetic GrainPro Stuffing

Direct container stuffing inside sealed bays to prevent moisture absorption in maritime transit.
